name: Credit spreads
summary: US high-yield spreads 3.63% on 23 Nov, down from a one-year high of 3.76% on 20 Nov; inside the 4% line
state: The US high-yield option-adjusted spread was 3.63% on 23 Nov, the latest reading, down from its one-year high of 3.76% on 20 Nov but 25bp wider on the month (FRED). The level and the monthly change remain inside the 4% and 100bp Watch lines, so Normal holds.
for_you: Lower-rated companies are paying slightly more to borrow than a month ago. Spreads remain below the levels usually associated with credit stress.
rubric_hit: HY OAS 3.72% below the 4% Watch line
why: High-yield spreads show how much lenders demand to fund weaker companies — an early warning of defaults and credit crunches.
drivers: Default expectations, risk appetite, rates, private-credit stress, fund outflows.

rubric.alert: HY OAS > 6.0%, or widened > 200bp in a month.
rubric.watch: HY OAS 4.0–6.0%, or widened > 100bp in a month.
